title: Smallness of modules with prescribed local models on a small ringed site
statement: Fix a Grothendieck universe $\mathcal V$ [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal C$ be a $\mathcal V$-small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] with finite limits and terminal object $1$, and let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings whose section sets belong to $\mathcal V$. Module sheaves have section sets in $\mathcal V$ and mean the sectionwise modules of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For every object $U$ of $\mathcal C$, fix a $\mathcal V$-small set $I_U$ and a family $(B_{U,t})_{t\in I_U}$ of module sheaves over $R|_U$ on the slice site $\mathcal C/U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Let $\mathcal P$ be the class of $R$-module sheaves $M$ for which there is a covering family $\{U_j\to1\}_j$ and indices $t_j\in I_{U_j}$ with $M|_{U_j}\cong B_{U_j,t_j}$. Then $\mathcal P$ is $\mathcal V$-essentially small: there is a set $S\in\mathcal V$ and a family $(M_s)_{s\in S}$ of members of $\mathcal P$ such that every member of $\mathcal P$ is isomorphic to some $M_s$. No Noetherian, scheme, finite-generation or effectivity-of-arbitrary-descent-data hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: For a fixed presheaf Q of R-modules, the class of module sheaves M whose underlying presheaf embeds into Q is essentially small. Mathlib PresheafOfModules.wellPowered makes Subobject Q small in the section universe. Restrict that small type to the subobjects isomorphic to underlying presheaves of sheaves and choose one realizing sheaf for each. Any embedding determines such a subobject, and Subobject.underlyingIso identifies its source with the chosen subobject. The fully faithful forgetful functor lifts the presheaf isomorphism between two realizations to a sheaf isomorphism. This is implemented by the proved private helper essentiallySmall_embeds, and uses choice only inside a theorem proof, not to supply any undefined object.

proof.text: The type of codes (S,t), where S is a subset of the small object type and t assigns to each U in S a label in I_U, is small in the fixed universe. For each code form Q(S,t) as the small product of the right direct images of B_{U,t(U)} under the slice projections. Mathlib overPushforwardOverAdj supplies the adjunction from slice restriction to this direct image, using binary products in C. Mathlib constructs the actual sheaf products and shows the forgetful functor preserves finite limits. No descent datum or effectivity assertion is involved.

proof.text: For a locally prescribed M, start with its witnessing indexed cover and take S to be its object support. For each U in S choose an occurrence of U in the original cover, with its model label and local trivialization. Transpose the local trivialization through overPushforwardOverAdj. The product of these transposed maps gives a morphism phi:M -> Q(S,t). The original cover, including all repeated objects, remains available; no claim that the support is itself a covering in the precoverage is made.

proof.text: The morphism phi is monic. If a,b:L -> M have a phi = b phi, compose with each product projection. Naturality of the adjunction and cancellation of each local trivialization imply that the restrictions of a,b to each object of S agree. In particular they agree over every member of the original indexed cover. For each W pull back that original cover along W -> 1, using IsSiteForCoverings. At each member of the pulled-back cover evaluate the equality on the corresponding object over a cover member; naturality and the uniqueness part of the sheaf condition then identify a_W,b_W. This proves a=b, including for empty covers. The proved private helper hom_ext_over_cover carries out this separatedness argument directly with Presheaf.IsSheaf.hom_ext_ofArrows.

proof.text: The forgetful functor from module sheaves to presheaves preserves finite limits, so the underlying presheaf map of phi is monic. Apply step 1 to the fixed underlying presheaf of Q(S,t) for each code. The supremum over the small code type of those essentially small object properties is essentially small, by Mathlib ObjectProperty instances. Step 3 puts every locally prescribed module in that supremum, and ObjectProperty.EssentiallySmall.of_le gives the stated conclusion. All sheaf and module universes and all hypotheses remain those of the original statement.

Step 1: Hom sets inject into a product over the small slice of maps between V-valued section sets. Step 2: the codes (K ⊆ Ob C, labels, isomorphisms g_UV on fixed products U×V) form a set in V, built from a power set, small products and unions, with no cocycle condition. Step 3: each M has a code; one occurrence is chosen per object and the original indexed cover is kept, so no repetition deletion is assumed (consistent with the reindexing-only site convention). Step 4: a_V=g a_U and b_V=g b_U give b_V^{-1}a_V=b_U^{-1}a_U; I checked the order of composition, and the self-overlap U×U is covered by g_UU. Step 5: lem-pur-sheaf-hom-cover-gluing (Stacks 03EM via 04TQ, sites.tex l.5637 read) glues the maps and their inverses on C/1=C, and its uniqueness gives inverse isomorphisms. Its hypotheses hold: R is commutative, finite limits give the overlaps, the cover is of 1. Step 6: representatives are chosen for the realized codes S ∈ V. Edge cases checked: empty I_U, an empty cover of 1 (modules are 0), singleton cover, repeated members, non-monic cover arrows. rg found no duplicate in the DAG. The gluing nodes for open covers and for étale sites are specialisations. Tool_use lem-pur-sheaf-hom-cover-gluing is accepted as a generic off-unit black box.
